findings.title: Retry-count delete branch is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body:
The second branch of the `deleteMany` OR filters only on `retryCount > 1`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` condition. The SMS cron job will therefore delete any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, …) whose `retryCount` exceeds 1.

Today only this handler increments `retryCount`. But the column is generic on the model, so the moment the email or WhatsApp schedulers adopt it, this job will silently wipe their reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to this branch (and probably `scheduled: false`).

findings.title: Unguarded update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
findings.body:
The new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the `catch` block (and the one in the `else` branch) is not itself guarded. If it throws, the exception escapes the loop and the handler fails. This can happen if the reminder was deleted or cancelled concurrently (P2025, record not found) or on a transient DB error.

All remaining reminders in the batch are then skipped and the original scheduling error is never logged, because the `console.log` comes after the update. Log first, and wrap the increment in its own try/catch (or use `updateMany`).

findings.title: Reminders with no message or recipient are never counted as failures
findings.body:
When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is null, the code takes neither branch and `retryCount` is not incremented. A missing number on the booking is one of the main permanent-failure causes this PR targets.

Such reminders keep being picked up and reprocessed by every cron run until their scheduled date passes, which is exactly the behaviour the PR intends to stop. Increment `retryCount` (or delete the reminder) in this case too.

findings.title: Unindexed retryCount predicate in OR may force a full table scan
findings.body:
The `deleteMany` now ORs the indexed `(method, scheduledDate)` condition with `retryCount > 1`, and `retryCount` has no index. Postgres will likely fall back to a sequential scan of the entire WorkflowReminder table, which covers all methods and is large, on every cron invocation.

Scoping the branch to `method = SMS`, which can use the existing `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index, or adding an index on `retryCount` would avoid this.
